add_block.new_heading: Planning catering guides step by step
new_paragraphs: Check the indicative price on each guide — most formats begin from AED 700 per person, with tasting menus from about AED 1,400 .
Send your date, guest count and venue — your catering guides proposal arrives.
Book catering guides about 2 weeks ahead off-peak, and 6 weeks ahead between November and March.
Confirm the catering guides menu 7 days before the date, with final numbers.
Ask about allergies when booking catering guides, well outside the final 48 hours .
Check how the team reaches the venue; catering guides setup begins about 2 hours before guests.
Plan on roughly 3 hours of catering guides service, and add 5% VAT to the total.

add_block.new_heading: How a guide differs from a blog article
new_paragraphs: A guide is built to be worked through; an article is built to be read. Guides are sequenced in the order decisions happen — venue before caterer, format before menu, guest count before price — and each one carries the deadlines attached to those decisions. That is why the checklists give you week counts instead of general advice.

The price guides do the opposite job: they explain how a number is assembled so you can read any quote, not just ours. Once you understand that labour instead of food drives most of the cost, comparing three proposals becomes clear instead of confusing.

new_paragraphs: Across every guide, four deadlines repeat. Book your caterer 8 to 12 months out for a peak-season wedding and 2 to 3 weeks for a standard dinner. Hold the tasting 3 to 4 months out for a large event, once the direction is set but while changes are still possible. Confirm the menu about 7 days before. Lock final guest numbers 7 to 14 days before, because that figure is what you are charged for whether or not every guest attends.

Miss those windows and your options narrow instead of vanish. The guides flag which decisions are genuinely time-critical and which can be left late without cost, so you spend your attention where it changes the outcome.

new_paragraphs: Each guide carries the same three commitments. Real published rates, so the figure in a guide matches the figure on the service page. Cited sources for anything regulatory, linked at the foot of the page. And an honest statement of what we do not know — where a price depends on your venue or your guest count, the guide says so instead of inventing a number.
Every catering quote in the UAE carries 5% VAT, and licensed operators work to the Dubai Municipality Food Code. Those two facts sit behind every figure in this section, and both are sourced below.

new_paragraphs: Figures and rules referenced across these pages come from official sources: the UAE Ministry of Finance (5% VAT on catering, in force since 1 January 2018), Dubai Municipality (Food Code, including requirements for food transportation and delivery vehicles and mandatory food-handler training), and Weather and Climate (Dubai December averages of 27°C by day and 19°C at night). Confirm current requirements before you book.

add_block.new_heading: If you only read one section
new_paragraphs: Start with the price guide, then the checklist that matches your event. Between those two you will have the number, the sequence and the deadlines — which is most of what planning an event requires. Everything else in this section refines a decision you have already framed.

A note on how to use the figures. Every rate here is a published myCHEF rate, so it will match the service pages exactly. What it will not do is predict your final total, because that depends on your guest count, your venue and your service format. Use the guides to understand how the number is built, then send your brief for a figure that applies to your event instead of to an average one. Proposals come back itemised, with the 5% VAT shown as its own line.

If a guide states a figure you intend to budget against, check the sources line at the foot of that page first. Every regulatory claim carries a link to the authority it came from, so you can confirm a tax rate or a food-safety rule yourself instead of relying on a caterer to summarise it accurately for you.

Which guide is suited to your event depends on the format — start with the price guide if you are budgeting, or a checklist if the date is set. Related: browse the full catering services in Dubai, compare our packages and prices , or look at corporate catering, party catering and luxury home catering by occasion. If you are searching for a caterer or catering company near me, a vetted chef and an itemised cost estimate are a message away — tell us the event, the menu and the guest count and you can hire the right team for the food, whether the budget is affordable or fully luxury.
